interest: This document provides valuable insight into the archival tracking and colonial mobilization policies of the Japanese Empire on the eve of the Pacific War. Specifically, it notes the planned introduction of voluntary military service in Taiwan in 1942, tracing the policy's lineage back to the 1938 volunteer enlistment system instituted in colonial Korea (Chosen). For historians, it illustrates both the incremental steps Japan took to draw colonial populations into its military apparatus and the close monitoring of Japanese press reports and cabinet decisions by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and U.S. diplomats in Tokyo.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46) classified under decimal file 894.2221, concerning enlistment in the Japanese Army. The sheet catalogs an incoming telegram (Telegram No. 857) sent on June 21, 1941, by United States Ambassador to Japan Joseph C. Grew to the Department of State's Division of Far Eastern Affairs. The entry records Japanese press reports announcing a cabinet decision to establish a voluntary military service system in Taiwan the following year, mirroring the volunteer system instituted in colonial Korea in 1938.

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet recording a 1941 telegram from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding Japanese Cabinet plans to introduce voluntary military service in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: This State Department List of Papers sheet (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, indexes documents filed under decimal number 894.2221 relating to Japanese Army enlistment. It records a telegram (No. 857) sent from Tokyo by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew on June 21, 1941, addressed to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. The summary notes press coverage of a Japanese Cabinet decision to establish a voluntary military service system in Taiwan the following year, following the model implemented in Korea in 1938.
